title: Expectations
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of expecting God's promises to be fulfilled, using the example of Simeon who waited for the Messiah. He encourages believers to look beyond symptoms and circumstances to God's Word, and to claim their healing through faith in Christ's atonement.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of influence, using the example of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how one's life and actions affect others. He emphasizes the importance of sincerity, humility, and adherence to God's Word over popularity or organizational loyalty, warning against pride and the loss of spiritual influence.

title: Letting Off Pressure
summary: William Branham speaks on the pressures of modern life and the need for a refuge in Christ. Using the Old Testament cities of refuge and the Passover as types, he emphasizes that true safety and relief from pressure come only by being under the Blood of Jesus, not by church membership or denominational affiliation.

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, and the Syrophoenician woman to illustrate the importance of persistent faith. He encourages believers to hold fast to God's Word despite opposition and to remain steadfast in their faith.

title: A Trumpet Gives an Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham speaks on the uncertainty of worldly systems—government, politics, home life, and church organizations—contrasting them with the certainty of God's Word. He emphasizes that the Bible is the only sure foundation, and believers must be trained to recognize the clear sound of the Gospel trumpet, standing firm on God's promises.
themes: faith and trust in God's promises

title: The Evening Messenger
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of the evening messenger, drawing from Zechariah 14:6-7. He discusses how God sends a prophet at the end of each age to call His people back to the Word, and how the current age is the end time where light will come in the evening.

title: Awakening Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus calming the storm, using the disciples' fear and lack of faith as a lesson for believers today. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that He is present with His people even in times of trouble. Branham encourages the congregation to trust in the Word and the Spirit rather than being flustered by circumstances.

title: Spirit of Truth
summary: William Branham preaches on the Holy Spirit as the Spirit of Truth who guides into all truth and shows things to come. He shares testimonies of visions and healings, emphasizing that God is interested in all creation and that believers must yield to the Holy Spirit.

title: The Voice of God in This Last Days
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to hear the Voice of God amidst the many confusing voices of the last days—political, Hollywood, philosophical, and false religious voices. He uses the examples of Samuel, Noah, Moses, and Adam to show how hearing and obeying God's Word changes lives and brings judgment on the world.

title: Just One More Time, Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Samson as a warning to the modern church, particularly the Pentecostal movement, which he argues has fallen into the same traps of glamour, organization, and compromise with the world. He calls for a return to the power of the Holy Spirit and the Word of God.

title: Zacchaeus, the Businessman
summary: William Branham tells the story of Zacchaeus, a wealthy tax collector who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. He uses this narrative to encourage businessmen and others to seek Jesus earnestly, regardless of social pressure or personal cost, and emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: Remembering The Lord
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of remembering the Lord through communion and the examples of biblical figures who remembered God's faithfulness. He emphasizes that true communion is communing with God and waiting for His response, and he encourages believers to stand firm on God's Word despite worldly pressures.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham speaks to a businessmen's breakfast about making the best investment—eternal life in Jesus Christ. He contrasts the rich young ruler who turned away because the cost was too great with the need for sincere, Word-based faith. Branham warns against gambling with religion, organizational pride, and worldly attachments that hinder true discipleship.

title: An Absolute
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of having an absolute in life, using Christ and His Word as the ultimate anchor. He illustrates through personal stories and analogies that every area of life requires a final authority, and for believers, that must be Christ, who is the same as His Word.

title: A Door In A Door
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast in Tucson, using the metaphor of a door to discuss Christ's knocking at the heart of the Laodicean church. He emphasizes the importance of recognizing God in unusual ways and places, and urges believers to open their hearts to Jesus.

title: A Absolute
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of having an absolute—something unchanging to anchor one's faith—especially in times of crisis. He uses biblical examples like Noah, Moses, Daniel, and Paul to illustrate how God's Word is the ultimate absolute that never fails. The sermon is part of a series of prayer meetings for two children facing death, urging believers to pray with unwavering faith in God's promises.

title: The Breach Between The Seven Church Ages And The Seven Seals
The First Seal
summary: William Branham begins the study of the Seven Seals, focusing on the First Seal of Revelation 6. He emphasizes that the Book is sealed and can only be opened by the Lamb, and that the mysteries are revealed in the last days. He warns against denominationalism and stresses the importance of being ready for the Rapture.

title: The Second Seal
summary: William Branham opens the service with prayer and introduces the study of the Second Seal from Revelation 6:3-4. He discusses the four horsemen, emphasizing that the white horse rider represents the antichrist spirit in three stages. He connects the revelation of the seals to the last days and the role of prophets, citing Amos 3:7. Branham also shares personal testimonies of supernatural events and warns against false impersonations of true spiritual movements.

title: The Third Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Third Seal from Revelation 6:5-6, describing the black horse and its rider with a pair of balances. He contrasts the fall of the natural Eve with the fall of the spiritual Eve (the church) at the Nicaea Council, warning against substituting man-made creeds for God's Word.

title: The Sixth Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Sixth Seal from Revelation 6:12-17, comparing it with Matthew 24 to show the judgment that comes after the Church is taken. He discusses the martyrs under the altar, the hundred and forty-four thousand Jews, and the great earthquake and cosmic disturbances that mark the beginning of the Tribulation period.

title: The Seventh Seal
subtitle: 63-0324E
summary: In this closing sermon of the series on the Seven Seals, William Branham discusses the Seventh Seal from Revelation 8:1, emphasizing the silence in heaven. He explains the interval between the Sixth and Seventh Seals, focusing on the sealing of the 144,000 Jews from the tribes of Israel during the Tribulation period, and distinguishes this from the Gentile Bride. He also reflects on the week's services and the importance of divine revelation.

title: God Hiding Himself In Simplicity
summary: William Branham speaks on how God hides Himself in simplicity, revealing Himself to the humble rather than the wise. He emphasizes that faith in God's Word, not education or science, is the path to knowing God, and that the Church must stay behind the Word.
themes: The Word of God as the standard

title: Victory Day
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of victory, contrasting worldly victories with the spiritual victory found in Christ. He emphasizes focusing on the innocent substitute, Jesus Christ, and warns against jealousy and division that lead to conflict.
themes: Unity in the Body of Christ

title: Look
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of 'Look,' urging believers to focus their faith on Jesus Christ and the Word of God. He uses analogies like a camera's range finder and a rifle's accuracy to illustrate the need to zero in on God's promises, emphasizing that the same power that worked in the apostles is available today through the Blood of Christ.
themes: The Word as the focus of faith
Cleansing by the Blood of Christ

title: Come, Follow Me
summary: William Branham speaks to young people about the importance of following Jesus Christ, using the story of the rich young ruler as a cautionary tale. He emphasizes that Eternal Life is not inherited but must be accepted through a born-again experience, and warns against rejecting the call of Christ for worldly possessions or popularity.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham opens a four-night campaign in Tucson, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses how to identify Christ through His works and the Scriptures, and encourages believers to seek a personal encounter with the living God.

title: Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for genuine faith and the demonstration of God's power, using the examples of Jonah and Solomon to show that Jesus Christ is greater than both. He challenges the congregation to look beyond symptoms and believe in the resurrection power of Christ, which is present today.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham preaches on the human longing to see God, explaining that God can be seen in His universe, His Word, His Son, and His people. He uses personal stories and nature illustrations to demonstrate God's presence and faithfulness.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus walking on water, using the disciples' testimony meeting on the sea as a backdrop. He encourages believers to have faith, separate from man-made doctrines, and let the life of Christ produce His works in them.

title: Conferences
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of conferences, drawing parallels between world conferences and God's conferences throughout Scripture. He emphasizes the need for unity among believers and the power of faith, sharing personal anecdotes and testimonies of healing.

title: Standing In The Gap
summary: William Branham returns to his home church after several months, sharing personal updates and plans for upcoming ministry trips. He dedicates several children to the Lord, emphasizing the biblical basis for child dedication over infant baptism. He also briefly mentions a healing testimony and announces his intention to preach on 'The Flashing Red Light Of His Coming' that evening.

title: The Flashing Red Light Of The Sign Of His Coming
summary: William Branham preaches on the signs of Christ's coming, comparing the days of Noah to the present time. He discusses the multiplication of people, the increasing beauty of women, and the moral decay as flashing red lights signaling that the end is near.

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' using the story of King Ahaziah who sought Baal-zebub instead of God, and Jeremiah's lament about no balm in Gilead. He argues that God's remedy for sin—the Blood of Jesus—is still available, but people refuse it due to stubbornness and fear of losing popularity. He calls for a return to the Word and a Spirit-filled life.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
O Lord, Just Once More
summary: William Branham preaches on the state of the Pentecostal church, using the story of Samson as a symbol of a fallen church that has lost its spiritual power by compromising with the world and organizing into denominations. He calls for a return to the original Pentecostal experience and warns against hybrid Christianity that lacks the genuine Spirit of God.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the sign of the resurrection and the greater works of Christ, comparing the faith of the queen of Sheba and the repentance of Nineveh to the present generation's need to accept God's gift of the Holy Spirit.

title: Is Your Life Worthy Of The Gospel?
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the great supper, warning against making excuses to reject God's invitation. He traces how nations and individuals have spurned the Holy Spirit's call, leading to judgment, and urges believers to live lives worthy of the Gospel by following Christ daily.
themes: Seal of God vs. mark of the beast

title: The Indictment
summary: William Branham delivers a sermon titled 'The Indictment,' in which he charges the denominational churches of his day with crucifying Jesus Christ afresh by rejecting the Word of God and clinging to creeds and organizations. He draws parallels between the religious leaders who crucified Christ physically at Jerusalem and modern churches that spiritually crucify Him by refusing to accept the full revelation of the Word. Branham argues that the same spirit of jealousy, spiritual blindness, and compromise is at work today, and he calls for a return to the sole authority of Scripture under the shed blood of Christ.

title: Communion
subtitle: 63-0707E
summary: William Branham leads a communion service, emphasizing self-examination and holiness before partaking. He reads from 1 Corinthians 11, explaining the importance of discerning the Lord's body and living a life worthy of the Gospel. The service includes prayers for forgiveness and sanctification of the bread and wine.

title: Why Cry? Speak!
summary: William Branham preaches on Exodus 13-14, focusing on God's command to Moses to stop crying and speak to the people to go forward. He draws parallels between Moses' calling and the present-day church, emphasizing the need for a personal encounter with God that anoints faith and brings supernatural reality to the Word.

title: Humble Thyself
subtitle: 63-0714E
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of humility and unity among believers, urging the congregation to confess faults, love one another, and work together in harmony. He anticipates a healing service and the manifestation of the Third Pull, emphasizing that God exalts the humble.

title: A Prisoner
summary: William Branham preaches on Paul's declaration of being 'a prisoner of Jesus Christ,' emphasizing total surrender to God's will and the Word. He contrasts being yoked to Christ versus being bound by personal ambition or denominational ties, urging believers to become prisoners to Christ alone.

title: He Cares. Do You Care?
summary: William Branham speaks on God's care for humanity, emphasizing the Holy Spirit as the Comforter who continues Christ's work. He addresses the lack of sincerity in modern society and the church, urging genuine confession and faith for healing and salvation.

title: God Doesn't Call Man To Judgment Without First Warning Him
summary: William Branham preaches on God's nature to always warn before judgment, using Hezekiah, Jonah, and Amos as examples. He emphasizes the urgency of the present hour and the need for repentance, drawing parallels to the end times.

title: Christ Is The Mystery Of God Revealed
summary: William Branham teaches that the entire Bible is the revelation of God's mystery in Christ, hidden from ages but now revealed to saints. He emphasizes that Christ is the image of the invisible God and the fullness of God dwells in Him, and that believers must continue in faith grounded and settled.
themes: Christ as the Image of God

title: There Is Only One Way Provided By God For Anything
summary: William Branham preaches that God has only one way to accomplish anything, and any deviation from that way is perversion. He uses examples from nature, such as hybrid seeds and the migration of geese, to illustrate how man's attempts to improve upon God's ways lead to corruption. He emphasizes that the only way to eternal life is through Jesus Christ, the Word made flesh, and that believers must cry out for the promises of God until they are fulfilled.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Spirit

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of a paradox as a miracle that seems incredible but is true. He uses biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, the feeding of the five thousand, and the virgin birth to illustrate that God is still performing paradoxes today through the new birth and the Holy Spirit.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the virtue of perseverance, using the example of the Syrophoenician woman who persisted in seeking Jesus' help for her daughter. He emphasizes that true faith is based on God's Word and leads to persistence despite obstacles, and he encourages believers to hold fast to God's promises.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham uses the story of the rich young ruler to discuss the concept of spiritual investments, urging believers to invest in eternal life through Jesus Christ rather than worldly possessions or denominational affiliations. He contrasts the Laodicean church age with the opportunity for true conversion and the new birth.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of influence, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate how even godly people can fall when they become self-sufficient. He emphasizes the importance of humility, reverence for God, and the need for Christians to live righteously as examples to others.

title: Once More
subtitle: 63-0804A
summary: William Branham uses the story of Samson to draw a parallel with the modern church, which he sees as having lost its spiritual power by compromising with the world and denominationalism. He calls for repentance and a return to the Word of God, urging believers to cry out for a revival of the Holy Spirit's power.

title: Calling Jesus On The Scene
summary: William Branham preaches on Mark 4:35-41, using the story of Jesus calming the storm to illustrate that believers have Jesus in their ship (their lives) and can call on Him in times of trouble. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His Word is the remedy for every problem.

title: The Uniting Time And Sign
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of discerning the signs of the times, emphasizing that God gives signs to believers. He draws parallels between the rejection of Jesus by the Jews and the current rejection of God's Word by churches uniting in ecumenical movements, warning of coming judgment.

title: How Can I Overcome?
summary: William Branham encourages believers to overcome the world by yielding to Christ, using examples from Noah, Daniel, and Lot. He emphasizes that true overcoming comes through the Holy Spirit, not human effort, and warns against becoming spiritually stagnant in the Laodicean church age.

title: Perfect Faith
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of perfect faith as a substance, not imagination, that comes by hearing the Word of God. He emphasizes that believers must recognize their position in Christ and have unwavering confidence in God's promises, illustrated through biblical examples and personal testimonies of healing.

title: Desperations
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of desperation in seeking God, using biblical examples like Jacob and Hezekiah. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the Token of the Blood applied, and that true faith requires love and fervent prayer.

title: Pardon
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of pardon through the blood of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that true pardon requires acceptance and sincerity, not mere ritual or tradition. He contrasts the Old Testament blood sacrifices with the New Testament reality of Christ's sacrifice, urging believers to display the token of the Holy Spirit in their lives.

title: Go, Wake Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus calming the storm, emphasizing that Christ is present with believers in every trial. He encourages the congregation to recognize Jesus' presence and to have faith in His power to calm life's storms, just as He did on the Sea of Galilee.

title: Souls That Are In Prison Now
summary: William Branham preaches on the fate of souls imprisoned in hell, drawing from visions he experienced as a youth and recent observations of modern women's appearance that reminded him of those visions. He explores the biblical passages in Jude, 2 Peter, and 1 Peter about angels and spirits in prison, and questions whether current times reflect the judgment he foresaw.

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings by expressing his desire to see Jesus Christ, not just hear about Him. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers should reflect His life. Branham contrasts true Christianity with reliance on education, entertainment, or religious dress, urging a return to the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Sign Of This Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the signs of the times, emphasizing that as in the days of Noah and Sodom, the last days will be marked by God's judgment and the manifestation of His Spirit in human flesh. He warns against seeking signs for entertainment and calls for genuine faith in the finished work of Christ.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of influence, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah from Isaiah 6. He emphasizes that Christians must be careful of their influence on others, avoid pride, and keep their eyes on God rather than on fallible humans. The sermon calls for reverence, humility, and staying in one's God-given position.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham speaks to businessmen in New York City about the investment of eternal life. He contrasts worldly investments with the assurance of salvation through Jesus Christ, using the story of the rich young ruler and examples from Noah and Daniel.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using biblical examples such as the Canaanite woman, Noah, Moses, David, and Samson. He encourages believers to persist in trusting God's Word despite opposition or lack of immediate results, and concludes with a prayer line for the sick.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit
the church as a reflection of Christ

title: Once More
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between Samson's fall and the modern church's loss of spiritual power. He laments that the church has compromised with the world, lost its spiritual sight, and become captive to denominational systems, just as Samson was captured by the Philistines. He calls for a return to the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit.
themes: Return to the Word of God

title: I Am The Resurrection And Life
summary: A funeral sermon for a young Christian named Garnett, using nature's cycles of death and resurrection to illustrate the certainty of the believer's resurrection through Christ. Branham emphasizes that only those 'germitized' by the Holy Spirit will rise again, and comforts the bereaved with the hope of reunion.

title: What Shall I Do With Jesus Called Christ?
summary: William Branham opens with a prayer for the Kennedy family after the President's assassination, then transitions to a Sunday school lesson on the trial of Jesus before Pilate. He emphasizes that the religious system of the day rejected Christ despite knowing He was the Messiah, and draws parallels to modern times where denominational systems prevent people from accepting the truth of God's Word.

title: Three Kinds of Believers
summary: William Branham preaches on three categories of believers: true believers, make-believers, and unbelievers, using biblical examples such as Peter, Noah, Daniel, David, Abraham, Job, Joseph, Nathanael, and Bartimaeus to illustrate genuine faith that trusts God's Word despite opposition or impossibility.

title: The World Is Again Falling Apart
summary: William Branham speaks on the world's moral, political, and religious decay, comparing it to the time of Christ's first coming. He warns that the world is again falling apart and calls for a return to the anointed Word of God for the hour.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham gives a personal testimony of his recent experiences with God, including a supernatural encounter in the Colorado mountains where he commanded a storm to cease and it obeyed. He reflects on the burden he has carried for five years and shares a vision of his wife as a young woman, leading to a deeper sense of God's presence and guidance.

title: The Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the Passover token of blood in Exodus 12, explaining it as a type of Christ. He emphasizes that the Holy Ghost is the believer's token today, identifying those who have accepted Christ's sacrifice. Branham calls for sincerity and separation from the world as the end-time exodus approaches.

title: The Super Sign
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of the 'super sign' as God's supernatural intervention in human history, culminating in the incarnation of Christ and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in the Church. He contrasts worldly 'super' achievements with God's eternal sign of a virgin conceiving and God dwelling with man, emphasizing that God always sends a prophet as a sign before judgment.

title: Influence
summary: William Branham speaks to the young people of Shreveport, using the story of King Uzziah and the prophet Isaiah to illustrate the power of influence and the importance of staying in one's God-ordained place. He warns against pride and the danger of trying to take a position God has not given, emphasizing that God's Word is the ultimate standard.
themes: The Word of God as the standard

title: Go, Awake Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the account of Jesus calming the storm, using it as a metaphor for the church facing trials. He discusses three classes of people—believers, unbelievers, and make-believers—and encourages the congregation to recognize Jesus' presence in their midst, even when trouble arises.

title: Wedding Ceremony
summary: William Branham officiates a wedding ceremony, joining a man and woman in holy matrimony. He prays for God's blessing on the couple and reflects on the parallel between earthly marriage and the coming of Christ for His Bride.

title: An Absolute
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of having an absolute in the Christian life, using Paul's conversion as an example of meeting Christ as the ultimate tie post. He contrasts man-made absolutes with God's Word, which is the final authority for believers.

title: Just Once More, Lord
summary: In this closing sermon of a convention, William Branham uses the story of Samson to draw a parallel to the modern church, which he sees as having lost its spiritual power by compromising with denominational systems and abandoning the Word of God. He calls for a return to the original Pentecostal experience and a willingness to die to the world in order to regain God's power.

title: Why Little Bethlehem
summary: William Branham delivers a Christmas message explaining why God chose the small, humble town of Bethlehem for the birth of Jesus. He emphasizes that God works through the insignificant and humble to display His glory, contrasting worldly tinsel with the true meaning of Christmas. The sermon calls believers to humility and to abide in Christ, the Bread of Life.

title: We Have Seen His Star And Have Come To Worship Him
summary: William Branham speaks on the true meaning of Christmas, contrasting it with commercialism and Santa Claus. He examines the biblical account of the wise men, the star, and Joseph's dream, emphasizing that God reveals truth through His Word and supernatural signs.

title: God's Gifts Always Find Their Places
summary: William Branham reflects on the true meaning of Christmas, contrasting it with pagan traditions. He examines the gifts of the Magi—gold, frankincense, and myrrh—as symbols of Christ's deity, service, and death, emphasizing that believers should dedicate themselves wholly to God.

title: Church Order
summary: William Branham addresses church leaders on proper order and operation of the local church, covering roles of deacons, trustees, and pastor, handling of spiritual gifts like tongues and interpretation, Sunday school organization, and maintaining discipline. He emphasizes following Scripture and the need for orderly conduct in worship services.

title: There Is A Man Here That Can Turn On The Light
Look Away to Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks about the Third Pull being vindicated and identified, urging the congregation to remain faithful as the end times approach. He shares testimonies of healings and miracles, including the salvation of Hattie Wright's sons and the calming of a storm, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: The Presence Of God Unrecognized
summary: William Branham preaches on the unrecognized presence of God, drawing from Matthew 12:38-42. He emphasizes that God's presence is often missed because people are blinded by traditions and creeds, and he calls for a revival of faith to recognize God's work in the current age.

title: Trying To Do God A Service Without It Being God's Will
summary: William Branham discusses the importance of doing God's will rather than trying to serve God in one's own way, using the biblical account of Uzza touching the Ark as an example. He shares personal experiences, including visions and encounters with angels, to emphasize that God's methods must be followed precisely. The sermon also touches on denominationalism, the Seven Seals, and the need for unity among believers.

title: Things That Are To Be
summary: William Branham speaks on the certainty of God's promises and the pre-planned nature of believers' lives. He emphasizes that Jesus has gone to prepare a place for His people, and that the earthly life is a type of the eternal one to come. The sermon contrasts the temporary, fallen civilization with the eternal Kingdom of God.
themes: The Bride of Christ as the Word

title: Leadership
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of leadership, using the story of the rich young ruler to illustrate how even a successful, religious person must accept Jesus Christ's leadership to inherit eternal life. He contrasts human leaders with divine guidance, emphasizing that true life comes only through Christ, the Word, and warns against relying on denominations or rituals.
